ai.title: Add writefile example to agent instructions
ai.summary: Added a simplified example response demonstrating correct `write_file` tool call syntax to `backend/src/system-prompt/agent-instructions.md`. Removed redundant instruction about using markdown for code display from `backend/src/tools.ts` as the new example clarifies tool usage. This internal change aims to improve agent consistency in applying file edits.

eli5.text: The instructions that guide how the system writes and edits files now include a clear example showing exactly how to format a file-saving action. The example demonstrates the correct syntax for requesting that a file be written or modified, so the system follows a consistent pattern when making changes. A reader flipping through the documentation would see a worked sample alongside the rules, instead of having to infer the format from text alone.

ai.title: Referrals page credits badge uses actual user data
ai.summary: Referrals page `CreditsBadge` now renders `data.referredBy.credits` and `r.credits` instead of static `CREDITS_REFERRAL_BONUS`. This ensures the badge reflects the actual credits balance of the referred user at the time of referral. Change applies to `web/src/app/referrals/page.tsx`.

eli5.text: When you or someone you referred opens the referrals page, the credit badge shown next to a referred person now displays that specific person's actual credit balance at the time they were referred, instead of a fixed bonus number. This affects anyone viewing the referrals list on the page, and you would notice that each entry shows a different, real credit amount rather than the same value repeated for every referral.

ai.title: Prompt Gemini to use tools better
ai.summary: Updated system prompts in backend/src/main-prompt.ts and backend/src/tools.ts to improve tool usage. Instructions now explicitly forbid XML attributes in favor of nested tags (e.g., <write_file><path>...) and clarify edit behavior to 'write' rather than 'highlight' changed parts. Minor typo fixes ('derivable') and stricter warnings about tool failure modes were also applied.

eli5.text: The assistant that helps power the system got slightly rewritten instructions about how to use its tools. If you watched it work, you'd notice it now writes out full snippets of code with clear markers like '... existing code...' instead of just highlighting changes, and it avoids using XML-style attributes in favor of nested tags. This mostly affects how reliably it edits files behind the scenes, making its instructions clearer and less error-prone for the parts of the system that apply its suggestions.

ai.title: Fix typo in git command safety rule
ai.summary: Corrected `git that` to `git commands` in system prompt. File: `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions told it not to run 'git that' without being asked, which was a typo. They fixed the typo to 'git commands', so the rule now clearly tells the assistant not to run git commands or scripts unless specifically asked. You would notice this only if you read the instruction text directly, which most people don't.

ai.title: Skip flaky main prompt integration test
ai.summary: The 'should add end_turn when LLM stream yields only text' test in `backend/src/__tests__/main-prompt.integration.test.ts` is now marked `it.skip`. Import statements were reordered alphabetically. This change isolates the flaky assertion from the CI pipeline.

eli5.text: A test that kept randomly failing in our automated checks has been paused so it no longer blocks new code from being added. Developers working on the backend will notice this specific test is skipped, and the remaining tests will run more reliably. This is internal housekeeping to keep our quality checks stable.
